en.title: Airbnb OA #6: Print Sentences as a Table
en.description:
Given n sentences and a fixed table content width width, print each sentence as one row of a bordered table.

A border line is `+`, followed by width+2 copies of `-`, followed by `+`. A sentence line is `| `, followed by the sentence itself, padded with spaces so the content takes exactly width characters, followed by ` |`.

For each sentence in order, output a border line and then its sentence line; finish with one more border line. When n=0, output nothing.
en.input:
The first line contains two integers n and width. Each of the next n lines contains one sentence (the whole line is the sentence content; it may contain spaces and may be an empty line).

0≤n≤100000, 1≤width≤300; sentences consist of printable ASCII characters and spaces, with length at most width.
en.output: When n>0, output a table of 2n+1 lines, each ending with a newline; when n=0, the output is empty. The output is compared character by character, so leading and trailing spaces of sentences must be preserved exactly.
en.explanation:
Example 1: width=55, so every border is + followed by 57 copies of - and then +; each sentence line pads the sentence with spaces to 55 characters.
Example 2: n=0, so there is no output.
Example 3: the two leading spaces of the first sentence, the empty second sentence, and the trailing space of the third sentence all count toward the content width as is.
hints: Read each sentence as a whole line; do not split it on whitespace.
Build the border string once and reuse it in the loop.
Do not forget the closing border at the end of the table, or the n=0 case.
